Phosphine-Catalyzed Remote 1,7-Addition for Synthesis of Diene
Carboxylates
Jiaxu Feng and You Huang *
Cite This: ACS Catal. 2020, 10, 3541 −3547 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: A phosphine-catalyzed remote 1,7-addition of vinyl allenoates has been developed, providing a series of 1,3-dienes
derivatives in high yields (up to 99%) and with good chemo-, regio-, and stereoselectivity. This reaction demonstrated that the
introduction of vinyl in allenoates e ﬀectively extended reaction types of phosphine-catalyzed nucleophilic addition of allenoates,
leading to concise synthesis of diene carboxylates. Notably, the enantioselective variant of this 1,7-addition can also be performed by
chiral phosphine catalyst.
KEYWORDS: γ-vinyl allenoates, phosphine, catalysis, remote 1,7-addition, synthesis, selectivity, dienes carboxylates
D
iene carboxylates are crucial skeletons which not only
widely exist in numerous natural products and bioactive
compounds1 such as bacteriostatic antibiotic Macrolactin A, 2
vitro antifugual activity (+)-papulacandin D ( Figure 1 ),3 but
also used as versatile building blocks in a number of organic
transformations.4 Although many methods have been developed
for their synthesis including transition-metal-catalyzed cou-
pling,
5 Wittig reaction, 6 isomerization of allenes, 7 and others, 8
most of them su ﬀered some undesired limitations such as
contamination of transition metals, stoichiometric amount of
byproducts, and sometimes long steps. Thereby, the develop-
ment of metal-free, catalytic, and concise methods for the
synthesis of diene carboxylates is still in high demand.
Phosphine-catalyzed reactions have received wide attention
during past decades, because they provide a powerful and metal-
free access to various C −C bonds formation in organic
synthesis, eliminating the contamination of metals in organic
products.
9,10 Major contributions in this ﬁeld focused on
electrophilic additions, in which the in situ formed zwitterionic
intermediate acts as a nucleophile to react with a certain
electrophile.
11 Later on, nucleophilic addition was found to be
feasible when appropriate pronucleophiles were used, a ﬀording
a new protocol for C −C bonds formation. 12 The pioneering γ-
umpolung additions of pronucleophiles to allenoates were
developed independently by Trost and Lu in the 1990s (Scheme
1a).
13,14
Later on, Huang and Lu’s group reported a new β-addition of
allenoates. 15 Despite these advances, more variations on
allenoates are still needed for the development of new types of
additions and versatile product motifs. In this context, Kwon and
co-workers introduced α-alkyl into allenoates, and achieved a
novel β′-umpolung addition for the synthesis of functionalized
acrylates (Scheme 1b).16 In 2009, we found the new reaction site
of δ-carbon of γ-methyl-substituted allenoates ﬁrst,17a then a
series of phosphine-catalyzed annulation reactions were
developed based on this discovery. Very recently, we designed
a new kind δ-sulfonamido-allenoates to develop a sequential [3
+ 3]/[3 + 3] annulation of allenoates;
17f to continue our
interests in phosphine-catalyzed reactions, 17 we envisioned a
new variation of allenoates for the synthesis of diene
carboxylates: installing a γ-vinyl group on allenoates to extend
the π-system of the zwitterionic intermediate to remote position,
thus allowing to construct a diene carboxylate motif ( Scheme
1c).

However, to enable this new reaction pattern, the following
challenges need to be considered: (1) regioselectivity control on
multiple reaction-sites such as nucleophilic α and γ positions,
electrophilic γ and ε positions after H abstraction. (2)
Appropriate pronucleophiles that enable both H abstraction
and subsequent addition step. (3) Di ﬃcult stereoselectivity
control of remote addition. With these concerns in mind, we
commenced our study by selecting 1-methyl-3-phenylindolin-2-
one ( 1a) and methyl hexa-2,3,5-trienoate ( 2a)a sm o d e l
substrates under mild conditions (Table 1). When the reactions
of 1a and 2a were performed in CHCl
3 at 30 °C, weakly
nucleophilic phosphines such as PPh 3 and other triaryl
phosphines showed good reactivity, providing the desired
product 3a in 48 −63% yields ( Table 1 , entries 1 −3), When
the diarylalkylphosphines Ph 2PEt was used, the reaction gives
56% yield ( Table 1 , entry 4), whereas strongly nucleophilic
phosphine, such as tributyl phosphine, signi ﬁcantly decreased
the yield ( Table 1 , entry 5). Then, we envisioned using
bifunctional phosphines bearing additional functional groups to
enhance the reactivity; thus, additional interactions between
phosphines and the substrates could accelerate the reaction rate.
Following this idea, we screened two bifunctional phosphines
(entries 6, 7), and ultimately, thiourea-derived phosphineP
2 was
found to be the optimal catalyst, a ﬀording the desired product
with signi ﬁcantly improved yield under the same conditions
(77%, entry 7). With P2 as the catalyst, other reaction
parameters such as solvents (entries 8 −12), temperatures
(entries 13 and 14) were systematically investigated, revealing
that the use of DCM as the solvent at 30 °C gave the highest
yield (98%, entry 10). When reducing the loading of catalyst to
10 mol %, a lower yield was obtained (86%, entry 15).
Meanwhile, a control experiment showed that without the
catalyst, no product was a ﬀorded and the starting material 1a
was recovered in 90% yield (entry 16). This result indicated that
the phosphine catalyst was essential. In this reaction, the
thiourea group of the bifunctional phosphines catalyst may play

With the optimal reaction conditions in hand, we turned to
examine the substrates scope by using various nucleophiles and
vinyl allenoates ( Table 2). We were pleased to ﬁnd that a wide
array of commercially available oxindole derivatives could react
eﬃciently under the optimized conditions, aﬀording the desired
diene carboxylates 3 in good yields (up to 99%). Di ﬀerent
substituents on the aryl rings at the 3-position of oxindoles were
examined, and the results showed that both electron-with-
drawing (3b and 3g) and electron-donating (3c, 3d, 3e, and 3f)
substituents at the para- and meta-position were tolerated,
aﬀording the products in good yields (93−99%). In addition, the
electron-donating group (Me) on the C-5 position of the
oxindole was also tolerated, providing diene carboxylate 3h in
99% yield. In contrast, the electron-withdrawing group (F) on
the same position led to 79% yield ( 3i), suggesting that
electronic eﬀect on the conjugated phenyl ring of oxindole was
more signi ﬁcant. Di ﬀerent 3-benzyl-substituted oxindole
derivatives also worked well in the reaction and a ﬀorded the
corresponding products of 3i, 3j, and 3l in good to excellent
yields (89 −99%); only the 3,5-dimethoxybenzyl-substituted
oxindole led to 69% yield (3m). All of the products give the E,E-
diene carboxylates that are highly stereoselective, and the
structure of 3l was unequivocally conﬁrmed by single-crystal X-
ray analysis (see the Supporting Information).
18
The protecting group on the nitrogen atom of oxindole can
also be replaced by the tert-butoxycarbonyl (3n and 3o), acetyl
(3p), benzyl (3q, 3z, and 3cc) groups, and the desired products
were obtained in 56 −75% yields. With oxindoles as
pronucleophiles, we next explored the generality of γ-vinyl
allenoates, and the results showed that the variation of ester
groups were well tolerated, a ﬀording the desired dienes
carboxylates 3r and 3s in the same 88% yield. Besides 3-
substituted oxindoles, other pronucleophiles were also compat-
ible with the current method. For example, a variety of 1,3-
dicarbonyl substrates a ﬀorded the corresponding products in
59−70% yields (3t, 3u, and 3v). Very interestingly, at the same
reaction condition, when using methyl acetoacetate bearing two
α-hydrogens as the pronucleophile, apart from that a single
addition product can be obtained in 42% yield, a double addition
product can also be produced in 29% yield ( 3w). In addition,
other cyclic and linear 1,3-dicarbonyl substrates were also
successfully compatible, providing single isomers in 58 and 74%
yields, respectively ( 3x and 3y). It should be noteworthy that
3aa, 3bb, and 3dd were produced in toluene at 100 °C.
Inspired by the double addition result of methyl acetoacetate,
we next investigated double addition of 1,3-dicarbonyl
compounds bearing two α-hydrogens with allenoates to form
bis(diene carboxylates) containing an all-carbon quaternary
center (Table 3). Because of high instability, these compounds
are diﬃcult to be prepared by other methods. Pleasingly, γ-vinyl
allenoates reacted with methyl 3-oxobutanoate and tert-butyl 3-
oxobutanoate, successfully providing the corresponding double
remote 1,7-addition products in 29 and 42% yields respectively
(4a and 4b). In addition, the Nazarov reagent has been proved
to be a suitable substrate, a ﬀording a corresponding product in
67% yield (4c). Ethyl 2-cyanoacetate was also compatible under
the reaction conditions, giving the desired product in 83% yield
(4d). Notably, indolin-2-one was also accommodated in this
reaction, albeit with moderate yield ( 4e). The structure of 4e
was unambiguously conﬁrmed by X-ray single-crystal analysis.
18

addition reaction. Although many chiral phosphines have been
checked, most of them led to either low yields or low ee values
(see the Supporting Information ). Only chiral phosphine

and 3z). This showcased that the steric e ﬀects might promote
this asymmetric reaction. Moreover, high enantioselectivites
were obtained for many products ( 3aa−3dd).
To demonstrate the utility of the reaction, gram −scale
reaction was conducted, a ﬀording 3l in 92% yield, without the
loss of eﬃciency (1.08 g, Scheme 2). To elaborate the potential
synthetic utility of the present protocol, several transformation
of diene carboxylates3l have been carried out (Scheme 2). Upon
treatment with N-phenylmaleimide, a Diels −Alder cyclo-
addition product 5 was a ﬀorded in 75% yield. The phenol
derivative 6 was prepared through a demethylation process.
Additionally, direct reduction of diene carboxylates 3l led to the
formation of allyl alcohol derivative 7, which underwent
oxidation reaction to give the corresponding aldehyde 9; the
aldehyde 9 can be converted to the triene derivative 10 by a
Witting reaction. Moreover, allyl chloride derivative 8 was
produced through Appel reaction, leaving ample room for
further application.
A deuterium labeling experiment was carried out to gain
insight into the mechanism. The result showed that α and β
positions can be deuterated in almost the same ratio of 56 and
50% respectively, whereas the ratios at γ and δ position were less
than 20%, which suggests that α and β positions in the
intermediate may display stronger nucleophilicity ( Scheme 3a).
Based on these results, a possible mechanism for this remote 1,7-
addition was proposed (Scheme 3b). First, nucleophilic addition
of phosphine catalyst to the
γ-vinyl substituted allenoate 2a
formed zwitterion A which can accomplish the equilibrium with
zwitterion A′. Zwitterion A is more stable than A′ because of the
π-electrons conjugate system, so the incorporation of deuterium
in γ (8%) is less than α (56%). Then, it deprotonated the
pronucleophile 1a to provide the intermediates B and C.
Subsequent nucleophilic addition of them at the remote ε
position resulted in the Zwitterion D that can also accomplish
the equilibrium with intermediate D′. Compared with D′, PPh

In summary, we have developed a phosphine-catalyzed
remote 1,7-addition of γ-vinyl-substituted allenoates, a ﬀording
a series of diene carboxylates in good to excellent yield with sole
regio- and stereoselectivity. When using 1,3-dicarbonyl
compounds bearing two α-hydrogens as the pronucleophiles,
the corresponding double remote 1,7-addition products were
obtained in moderate to good yields with an all-carbon
quaternary center, which are di ﬃcult to be synthetized by
traditional methods. The preliminary asymmetric version of this
remote addition can give the moderate to good yields and ee
values by using the chiral phosphine catalyst. The application of
the corresponding diene carboxylates for the synthesis of other
useful compounds were also demonstrated. The introduction of
vinyl into allenoates e ﬀectively extended reaction types of
phosphine-catalyzed nucleophilic additions of allenoates.
Exploring more applications of this type of substrates is
currently underway in our lab.
